description: Figure 8(c) illustrates the branching ratio γB across a range of few-shot examples. The horizontal axis represents the number of few-shot examples, labeled “Number of Shots,” with categories ranging from 1 to 8, sorted in ascending order. The vertical axis represents the branching ratio γB, labeled “Branching Ratio γB,” with a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at 0.2 intervals.  Three distinct lines are plotted, each representing a different condition: “Minimal” in a solid blue line, “Correct” in a dashed orange line, and “Estimated” in a dash-dotted green line. The “Minimal” line begins at approximately 0.25 for 1 shot, increases to approximately 0.6 for 3 shots, and plateaus around 0.7 for the remaining shots. The “Correct” line starts at approximately 0.6 for 1 shot, rises to approximately 0.9 for 3 shots, and remains relatively stable around 0.9 for the rest of the shots. The “Estimated” line begins at approximately 0.4 for 1 shot, increases to approximately 0.7 for 3 shots, and then gradually increases to approximately 0.9 for 8 shots. No bars are visually emphasized.
